Estimate statistical distribution

Source: R/stats.R
est_dist.Rd

Determines whether grouped data are best represented by a normal, lognormal, or other candidate distribution.

est_dist(
  df,
  return_result = FALSE,
  alpha = 0.05,
  method = "sw",
  choices = c("norm", "lnorm"),
  min_n = 4
)

Arguments

df

Tidy groundwater data frame. Grouping determines the level at which distributions are estimated.

return_result

TRUE/FALSE.

alpha

Significance level.

method

Goodness-of-fit method passed to EnvStats::distChoose().

choices

Candidate distributions.

min_n

Minimum sample size required for estimation.

Value

A tibble with one row per group containing:

distribution

Selected distribution.

n

Number of non-missing observations used in estimation.

data

Nested data frame containing the observations used for the group.

result

EnvStats result object stored as a list-column when return_result = TRUE.

Details

The returned object retains the original grouped observations in a nested `data` list-column. This allows downstream functions such as prediction interval, tolerance interval, and control chart calculations to access the observations used for distribution estimation.

Examples

data("gw_data")

gw_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    location_id,
    param_name,
    default_unit
  ) %>%
  percent_lt() %>%
  est_dist()
#> Error in gw_data %>% dplyr::group_by(location_id, param_name, default_unit) %>%     percent_lt() %>% est_dist(): could not find function "%>%"
